Enantioselective Cyanoborylation of Allenes by N‑Heterocyclic
Carbene-Copper Catalysts
Zhenghua Li, Liang Zhang, * Masayoshi Nishiura, Gen Luo, * Yi Luo, and Zhaomin Hou *
Cite This: ACS Catal. 2020, 10, 11685 −11692 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: The simultaneous incorporation of both a cyano group and a boryl
unit into the C C double bonds of allenes in a regio- and stereoselective fashion
is of much interest and importance but remains a signi ﬁcant challenge. We report
herein a copper-catalyzed chemo-, regio-, and enantioselective cyanoborylation
of allenes, which a ﬀorded a family of valuable enantiopure β-boryl allyl nitriles.
The high enantioselectivity was achieved by installing of appropriate substituents
at the C2 and C6 positions of the naphthyl groups in our newly synthesized
N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands. The reaction mechanism has been clari ﬁed
by some stoichiometric reactions and computational studies. This work provides
an inspiring example of the development of selective catalytic reactions for the
synthesis of functional molecules through ﬁne-tuning the ligands in catalysis.
KEYWORDS: allenes, asymmetric catalysis, carbene ligand, copper, cyanoborylation
1. INTRODUCTION
The catalytic multifunctionalization of unsaturated C −C bonds
is a straightforward and e ﬃcient strategy for the assembly of
densely functionalized chemicals from simple starting materials.
In view of the tremendous applications of organoboron com-
pounds in various chemical transformations
1 and nitriles as
versatile intermediates for the synthesis of many biologically
active molecules,ﬁne chemicals, dyes, pigments, and polyamides,2,3
the direct cyanoborylation of allenes 4 in an enantioselective
fashion, which would lead to the simultaneous installation of
both a cyano group and a boryl group into a C C double
bond of the allene substrate, is of particular interest and
importance. However, the difunctionalization of the 1,2-orthogonal
CC double bonds in allenes often su ﬀers from regioselectivity
problems. Besides, chemoselectivity issues can also arise due to the
simultaneous existence of a number of reactive species. Although
several copper-catalyzed enantioselective borylative function-
alization reactions of allenes were reported recently,
5−11 the
enantioselective cyanoborylation12 of allenes has not been achieved
yet.
In 2009, Suginome et al. disclosed an early example of
palladium-catalyzed cyanoborylation of an allene compound
via a metal-cyanide intermediate to give an achiral β-cyano
allylborane in a relatively low yield ( Scheme 1A, i).
13 In 2016,
Montgomery et al. reported an elegant trifunctionalization of
allenes for the synthesis of β,γ-diboryl nitriles through sequen-
tial cyanoborylation and hydroboration ( Scheme 1 A, ii).
14
In this transformation, suppressing the overaddition of a copper
boryl species to the remaining C C double bond in the initial
cyanoborylation products was di ﬃcult. Therefore, the chemo-,
regio-, and enantioselective cyanoborylation of allenes still
remains a highly attractive research subject for the synthesis of
valuable molecules containing multiple synthetically important
functional groups, including a chiral nitrile unit, a boryl group,
and a C C double bond.

During our previous studies on the catalytic addition of
copper boryl species to alkynes, 15 aldehydes,16 and imines, 17
we became interested in the development of selective cyano-
borylation of allenes through copper boryl catalysis. Herein, we
report a copper-catalyzed chemo-, regio-, and enantioselective
cyanoborylation of allenes, which a ﬀorded β-boryl allyl nitriles
eﬃciently ( Scheme 1 B). The competing hydroboration of the
remaining C C double bonds after cyanoborylation was suc-
cessfully suppressed. The systematic adjustment of the substituents
on the C2 and C6 positions of the naphthalene moieties in our
newly prepared chiral N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands
enabled the direct synthesis of valuable enantiopure β-boryl
allyl nitriles, which could be readily elaborated into useful
organic molecules. This method shows excellent functional
group tolerability and is easy to scale up. Computational studies
revealed that the regioselectivity of borocupration is governed
by both the steric hindrance and electronic eﬀects. The enantio-
selectivity of cyanation is attributed to the steric e ﬀects of the
substituted naphthyl wingtips of the NHC ligand. The current
reaction represents an inspiring example of ﬁne-tuning of a
ligand enabling selective catalysis for the e ﬃcient synthesis of
complex molecules from simple feedstocks.
2. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
We began the research study with the investigation of various
ligands for the copper-catalyzed cyanoborylation of cyclo-
hexylallene 1a with bis(pinacolato)diboron (B
2(pin)2)18 and
electrophilic cyanation agent N-cyano-N-phenyl-p-toluenesul-
fonamide (NCTS) 19 (Table 1 ). Among all the tested copper
catalysts, the NHC-copper complex [(SIMes)CuCl] (SIMes =
1,3-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)imidazolin-2-ylidene) resulted in
the formation of desired cyanoborylation product 2a in high
yield and regioselectivity (entry 3). The formation of only 4%
of regioisomer 2a′ was detected. Remarkably, the catalyst
loading could be reduced to 5 mol % without signi ﬁcant erosion

of the C C double bond in 2a was successfully suppressed
(less than 4% of the trifunctionalization product was detected by
1H NMR analysis), in contrast withwhat was observed previously
in the trifunctionalization of allenes.14 Both [(IPr)CuCl] (IPr =
1,3-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)imidazol-2-ylidene) and [(IMes)-
CuCl] (IMes = 1,3-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)imidazol-2-ylidene)
gave lower yields, albeit comparable regioselectivities were
observed (entries 1 and 2). LiO tBu is the best among the
tested bases (entries 4 −6). The combinations of CuCl with a
series of phosphine ligands (entries 7 −14) were found to be
inferior to [(SIMes)CuCl].
Under the optimized reaction conditions ( Table 1, entry 4),
we investigated the substrate scope of the [(SIMes)CuCl]-
catalyzed cyanoborylation of a wide range of allenes ( Table 2).
The reactions of a variety of terminal allenes a ﬀorded the
desired cyanoborylation products 2a−y in good to excellent
yields selectively. Remarkably, functional groups such as silyl
ether, benzyl ether, thioether, alkene, alkyne, ester, heterocycle,
and halides (Br, Cl, and F) were compatible with the current
reaction conditions.
Considering the great importance of chiral nitriles, 2,3c,3d we
then investigated a large series of C2 symmetric NHC ligands
based on a chiral diphenylethylene diamine backbone for the
enantioselective cyanoborylation of allene 1a (Table 3). In the
presence of 5 mol % CuCl, the reactions using N-phenyl-
substituted NHC ligands L1−6 generally aﬀorded chiral nitrile
product (S)-2a regioselectively in good yields ( Table 3, entries
1−6). It is also encouraging that a moderate enantiomeric ratio
was achieved in the case of L6 (75:25 er, entry 6). When
employing NHC ligand L7 with naphthyl wingtips,
20 a slight
improvement of enantioselectivity was observed (77:23 er,
entry 7). It was proven that the introduction of methyl ( L8)o r
isopropyl ( L9) to the C2 position of naphthyl groups led to
the same enantiomeric outcome (entries 8 and 9). In order to
inspect the substituent e ﬀect at other positions, we synthesized
new NHC ligands L10−12, which features an alkyl group on
the C6 position of a naphthyl moiety. The reaction using L10
only showed a subtle improvement in the enantioselectivity
(79:21 er, entry 10). Replacing the methyl groups in L10 with
isopropyl groups, L11 led to a marked increase in the enan-
tiomeric ratio (88:12 er, entry 11). The introduction of bulkier
adamantyl to the C2 position of naphthyl groups, ligand L12
resulted in a slightly decreased enantiomeric ratio (86:14 er,
entry 12). The eﬀect of reaction temperature was then examined
by using ligand L11 (entries 13 −16). Performing the reaction
at −5 °C resulted in a higher enantiomeric ratio (93:7 er,
entry 14). The further examination of copper sources indicated
that the best enantioselectivity (96:4 er) could be obtained
when [Cu(CH 3CN)4]PF6 was used (entries 17 −19). While
10 mol % catalyst loading furnished ( S)-2a in high yield, a
lower yield was observed when 5 mol % catalyst was used
(entry 20).
After identifying L11 as the best candidate of ligands, we
then investigated the substrate scope of the asymmetric cyano-
borylation of allenes under the optimized reaction conditions
(Table 3 , entry 19). The results are summarized in Table 4 .
Using the substrates previously described in Table 2 , the new
enantiomerically selective catalyst system gave good to excellent

To demonstrate their synthetic utility, we explored a series
of reactions of the obtained densely functionalized chiral
nitriles, aﬀording a number of valuable molecules ( Scheme 2).
First, copper-mediated brominations of ( S)-2a or (R)-2d were
found to yield vinyl bromide containing chiral nitriles ( R)-3a
or ( R)-3b with the enantioselectivity retained ( Scheme 2 A).
21
The absolute con ﬁguration of ( R)-3b was determined by X-ray
crystallographic analysis. 22 The vinyl boronic ester group in
(S)-2a could also react with allyl alcohol to a ﬀord chiral nitrile
(S)-4 with a 93:7 enantiomeric ratio (Scheme 2B).23 Palladium-
catalyzed cross-coupling reaction of ( S)-2a with methyl
4-bromobenzoate resulted in the formation of tetra-substituted
alkene 5 with the isomerization of a C C double bond was
observed ( Scheme 2 C).
24

A possible reaction mechanism for this NHC-copper catalyzed
selective cyanoborylation of allenes is proposed as shown in
Figure 1 . The initial reaction between catalyst precursors and
LiOtBu would a ﬀord copper alkoxide [LCuO tBu], which upon
reaction with B 2(pin)2 could generate copper boryl complex
[LCuB(pin)]. Its subsequent regioselective borocupration of
allene substrate 1 would furnish allyl cuprate I. Further attack
of I to the C −N triple bond of NCTS with allylic transposition
via transition state TS would release β-boryl allyl nitrile product
2 along with copper imide II. Subsequent transmetallation
between II and LiO tBu would regenerate [LCuO tBu].
To get a deep understanding of the mechanistic details and
the selectivities of the current NHC-copper catalyzed cyano-
borylation reaction, DFT calculations were performed on the
reaction of cyclohexylallene 1a with B
2(pin)2 and NCTS
catalyzed by the SIMes-ligated copper catalyst. As shown in
Figure 2 , the coordination of an allene substrate 1a to
[(SIMes)CuB(pin)] ( A) could give the π-complex, and then,
the borocupration took place through the insertion of a C C
double bond of allene substrate 1a into a Cu −B bond. During
this step, there are four insertion manners, viz., 1,2-insertion
(TS1), 2,1-insertion (TS1a), 3,2-insertion (TS1b), and 2,3-insertion
(TS1c),27 which will aﬀord the corresponding intermediatesC, Ca,
Cb, and Cc. The results suggested that the 1,2-insertion via TS1
is the most favorable manner with the lowest energy barrier
of 15.7 kcal/mol, which is in agreement with experimentally
observed regioselectivity. This is mainly due to the smallest
sterics between allene substrate 1a and the SIMes ligand for
the 1,2-insertion manner in comparison with other pathways
(Figure S2 ). In addition, the nucleophilic boryl group is more
likely to couple with the π-electron de ﬁcient sp-C over the
sp
2-C of allene 1a.25c Therefore, both the steric and electronic
factors account for the regioselectivity of 1,2-insertion viaTS1.14b

To further understand the enantioselectivity in the case
of chiral NHC ligand L11, we performed the calculations on
the enantioselectivity-controlling step. It should be noted that
there are three diastereomers of ligand precursor L11. Thus,
three diastereomers of copper boryl species [L *CuB(pin)], i.e.,
(Ra,Ra)-A,( Ra,Sa)-A, and ( Sa,Sa)-A were ﬁrst calculated, and
it was found that they have almost the same thermodynamic
stability ( Scheme S1 ).
The calculated results with the ( Ra,Ra)-L11 ligand show
that the transition state ( Ra,Ra)-S-TS2 (leading to product
(S)-2a) is more favorable than ( Ra,Ra)-R-TS2 (leading to ( R)-
2a) by 2.1 kcal/mol, which is well in line with the experi-
mentally observed enantioselectivity ( Figure 3 ). Through
careful examination of the two cyanation transition states,
the enantioselectivity was found to be mainly originated from
the steric repulsion between the substituents of the substrates
and the chiral NHC ligand. As shown in Figure 3,i n( Ra,Ra)-
R-TS2, the shortest interatomic distance between an NHC
ligand and a boryl group or tosylate group is about 2.6 Å, while
the similar shortest interatomic distance is more than 3.0 Å in
the favored ( Ra,Ra)-S-TS2. As for the cases of ( Ra,Sa)-L11
and ( Sa,S
a)-L11 ligands, the cyanations via an S-TS2 manner
are also more preferred than an R-TS2 manner by 2.6 and
0.9 kcal/mol, respectively. Therefore, the same enantioselectivity
could be obtained with three diastereomers of ligand L11.
3. CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we have developed a copper-catalyzed chemo-,
regio-, and enantioselective cyanoborylation of allenes by the
use of a new chiral NHC ligand, which highlights the isopropyl
substituents at the C2 and C6 positions of the naphthyl
wingtips. The reactions of a wide range of allenes a ﬀorded the
enantiopure β-boryl allyl nitriles, which show broad synthetic
potentials. The unwanted overaddition of copper boryl species
to the remaining boron-activated C C double bonds after
cyanoborylation was successfully suppressed. Stoichiometric
reactions of NHC-Cu complexes were also carried out to prove
some mechanistic aspects. Computational studies found that
the stability of the borocupration transition states governs the
regioselectivity of the current reaction. Further DFT calculations
also revealed that the enantioselectivity was controlled by the
steric eﬀects of chiral NHC ligand L11. This method sets up an
enlightening model for the development of selective catalytic
processes through ﬁne-tuning ligand design.
